author: Cait Kontalis
title: This Little-Known Waterfront Town in Illinois Is Pure Magic - NewsBreak
text:
By Cait Kontalis ,
7 hours ago
There is a little-known waterfront town in Illinois that is so far north it touches the border of Wisconsin. On its east end, it borders Lake Michigan. Many folks visit Chicago and miss out on the hidden waterfront destination that is Zion, Illinois. With a picture-perfect beachfront, historic architecture, and many museums, Zion is one of the best small towns in Illinois to visit.
What To See and Do in Zion Photo by Peter Gorman via Flickr Creative Commons The highlight of Zion is its beachfront. The waterfront town is home to Adeline Jay Geo-Karis Illinois Beach State Park . This 6.5-mile stretch of sandy shoreline along Lake Michigan is the last remaining beach ridge shoreline in Illinois. Within the park, you’re treated to views of sand dunes, marshes, oak forests, and plenty of local wildlife. There are designated swimming areas for you to cool off in on a hot summer’s day.
In addition to nature, Zion offers stunning historic architecture. The historic Shiloh House is now a museum. This 25-room restored mansion was built between 1901 and 1902. Today, the museum is open to the public and features exhibits with items from the original owners and local Zion history. Visitors can also explore the Russell Military Museum . Guests can see a variety of military vehicles used in various conflicts.
Finally, Zion’s downtown area is filled with history. You can visit a historic spring called Esther’s Well and stroll along Shiloh Park. There are a variety of locally-owned restaurants and cafes to fuel up for your historic adventures. Some popular spots for a bite include the Lakefront Smokehouse, DaDa’s Soul, Honey Bee Cafe, and Coco’s Cafe and Pancake House. There’s also a variety of events that take place throughout the year, like farmers markets at Nostalgia Days, which features a car show.
Best Time To Visit Zion Photo by Mary Louise Eklund via Flickr Creative Commons
Zion offers things to do for everyone at every time of year. However, the summer is often the best time to take advantage of the fantastic beach access. Spring is also great, as the area is known for bird watching and wildflowers at Adeline Jay Geo-Karis Illinois Beach State Park. The fall brings classic foliage changes, and winter can bring a striking, icy beauty to the lakefront.
What To Know Before You Go Photo by MarieSchoblo via Flickr Creative Commons A day exploring Zion is plenty of time. About an hour drive from downtown Chicago, it’s the perfect way to complement your trip to the Windy City. Alternatively, Zion is less than an hour drive from Milwaukee, Wisconsin. You can easily turn that journey into a Chicago-to-Milwaukee road trip. Zion allows you to see the true, wild beauty of Lake Michigan without the noise of a big city. It’s important to note that the focus here isn’t on the city so much as it is on the nature. The town supplements its stunning lakefront, as the water is the true star of the show.
The small town of Zion often gets overlooked for those closer to Chicago. However, the small community has done a noteworthy job of preserving its historic downtown. The taste of history on top of the unbeatable beach ridge is something one can truly find nowhere else in the Land of Lincoln. Check it out for yourself on your next trip to Chicago or Milwaukee.
